name: Payesh
subtitle: rice cooked slowly down in milk with cardamom and date palm jaggery

ingredients.note: gobindobhog is traditional; any short-grain rice works
use 120g sugar instead if you cannot find it

prepNotes: Wash the rice and soak 20 minutes, then drain and toss with the 1 tsp ghee — this keeps the grains from clumping.
Use the heaviest pan you own and rinse it with water before adding the milk; the film of water stops the milk catching.
Chop the jaggery finely so it dissolves quickly at the end without needing extra heat.

steps.text: Bring the milk to a boil with the bay leaf and bruised cardamom, then lower to a bare simmer.
Simmer 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the skin from the sides back in, until it has reduced by about a quarter.
steps.tip: Scrape the sides. The reduced milk stuck there is the best part of the payesh.

steps.text: Add the drained, ghee-coated rice and the pinch of salt.
Cook on low for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 3-4 minutes so nothing sticks, until the grains are completely soft and the milk has thickened to the consistency of pouring cream.
steps.tip: It thickens a lot more as it cools, so stop while it still looks loose.

steps.text: Fry the cashews and raisins in a dry pan for 90 seconds until the cashews are gold and the raisins swell.
Stir them into the payesh and cook 2 minutes more.
Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 8-10 minutes — the surface should no longer be steaming hard.
steps.tip: This is the critical pause. Jaggery in hot milk will curdle the whole pot.

steps.text: Stir in the chopped jaggery and the sugar if using until fully dissolved. Do not put the pan back on the heat.
steps.tip: If it does split, whisk hard off the heat and it will usually come back together.

steps.text: Cool to room temperature, then chill at least 2 hours before serving.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated in a covered bowl. Serve cold or at room temperature; loosen with a splash of cold milk if it has set too stiff.
